description: Parent-source data for the provisional A1/A2/B/C parcel model. Corrected baseline: Frederick Buckler’s agricultural tenancy relates to Parcel B only; there was no tenancy of Parcel A. Mary Williams’s occupation and ownership claim to A2 were independent. The 1939 WGR–John Williams agreement/plan is associated with Parcel B only and its signature, execution and consideration are disputed. For 1955, distinguish the asserted legal scope of Order 14 (Parcel B only) from the physical taking (Parcel B, Parcel C and northern woodland A1); the farmhouse and garden (A2) remained occupied by Mary. These are the family’s corrected research positions; original instruments and plans remain the test.

map_reference.image_role: Photograph of a tithe schedule page, not a geographic map or selected parcel polygon
map_reference.overlay_status: No historic polygon is highlighted until the exact row and boundary are verified

parcel_model.label: Parcel A — north woods plus house and garden
parcel_model.description: Current working model: Parcel A comprises A1 (the northern woodland) and A2 (the farmhouse, buildings and garden). The green south of the house is outside Parcel A and is modelled separately as Parcel C. The family’s position is that the 1928 operation of a term in the 1877 agreement changed the relevant parcel interests and that Mary’s A2 occupation was an independent ownership claim, not a tenancy derived from Frederick.
parcel_model.limits: Analytical reconstruction, not a surveyed boundary or final legal determination. The original 1877 instrument, plan, 1928 evidence and title instruments remain essential to confirming extent and legal effect.

parcel_model.label: A1 — north woods
parcel_model.description: The current model places the northern woodland within Parcel A as A1. The family’s corrected reconstruction is that this woodland was physically taken on 4 July 1955, but was outside the asserted legal scope of Order 14, which concerned Parcel B only. The physical taking must not be confused with the land legally covered by the order.
parcel_model.limits: Compare the original 1955 order, warrant, execution return and 1961 woodland deed. Do not infer that A1 was included in Order 14 merely because the later account uses “whole farm”.

parcel_model.label: A2 — house, buildings and garden
parcel_model.description: The farmhouse, buildings and garden are A2, the house part of Parcel A. The family’s position is that Mary occupied and asserted ownership independently; there was no tenancy of Parcel A. A2 was not physically taken in the 4 July 1955 taking and was outside the asserted scope of Order 14.
parcel_model.limits: The original 1877 instrument, 1928 evidence, 1955 order and execution return, 1962 pleadings/order and 1982–83 registration files must be examined. Do not infer that Frederick’s Parcel B tenancy governed Mary’s A2 occupation.

parcel_model.label: Parcel B — eastern/right-hand fields
parcel_model.description: Parcel B is the eastern/right-hand agricultural fields. The 1939 WGR–John Williams agreement and plan are associated with Parcel B only. Frederick Buckler’s 2 February 1949 agricultural tenancy related to Parcel B, not Parcel A.
parcel_model.limits: The 1939 agreement’s attributed signature, execution, provenance and consideration/payment are disputed. The family alleges a signature mismatch and non-payment; neither forgery nor fraud is established without the original and corroborating evidence. The 1955 Order 14 is understood by the family to have had Parcel B as its legal scope.

parcel_model.label: Parcel C — green south of the house
parcel_model.description: Parcel C is the green south of Mary Williams’s house, separate from Parcel A and not included in the 1939 Parcel B agreement. The family’s corrected reconstruction places C among the land physically taken on 4 July 1955, although the asserted legal scope of Order 14 was Parcel B only.
parcel_model.limits: Check the VG41 application and map, the 1955 order/warrant/return and relevant conveyances. Do not fold C into Parcel A or assume physical taking proves it was within the order.

model_events.title: Northern woodland physically taken in 1955; order scope disputed
model_events.details: The family’s corrected reconstruction is that the northern woodland (A1) was physically taken on 4 July 1955, although the legal scope of Order 14 was Parcel B only. The order’s phrase “whole farm” must be read against the 1916 definition and the reported 1928 change arising from the 1877 agreement term. The original order, warrant, execution return and 1961 woodland deed must be compared.
model_events.status: Family’s corrected reconstruction; original order and execution records required

model_events.title: Alfred Thomas dies; Corporation bequest report and 1928 payment require reconciliation
model_events.details: The Dictionary of Welsh Biography dates Alfred Thomas, 1st Baron Pontypridd’s death to 14 December 1927; it identifies him as Daniel Thomas’s son and says he died unmarried. A secondary transcription of a 27 December 1927 newspaper report describes the “unofficial report” that the “bulk of his property” was left unconditionally to Cardiff Corporation and citizens. The original newspaper, will and grant have not been inspected. A separate research note cites a reported grant date of 8 March 1928 and London Gazette notice of 30 March 1928, p.2387; these details remain leads until the grant and Gazette entry are checked. The report does not identify the assets, and nothing currently establishes that Alfred’s estate included the Llandough house parcel. Equally, the absence of a located Llandough transfer does not prove that nothing passed to Cardiff Corporation. The 23 February 1905 Bute conveyance to Cardiff Corporation, separately listed in the WA231076 file, is a competing title-chain lead that must be inspected alongside any Thomas estate transfer.
model_events.status: Death date and identity supported by the Dictionary of Welsh Biography; 1927 Cardiff Corporation bequest is an unofficial secondary report; grant reference is unverified; any Llandough land effect unknown.

model_events.title: Mary recalls a 1928 final rent payment attributed to Alfred Thomas
model_events.details: Mary (Nancy) Williams’s c.1974 statement says that when quarry machinery was removed in 1928, the last rent payment was made “to Alfred Thomas the son of Daniel Thomas”; she says her father made it, the rent was about £4 per annum, and she saw the receipt. Alfred had died on 14 December 1927, so the statement does not establish a personal payment to him while alive in 1928. Possible explanations include payment to his estate, executor or authorised agent, a receipt continuing to use Alfred’s name, or a remembered date/payee error; none is proved. The receipt is not located. The 10 November 1925 sale catalogue for Llandough Quarry plant and tramlines (Glamorgan Archives DSA/12/4888) and the 1927 obituary wording that the limeworks were carried on by Alfred and then given up are separate chronology leads; a sale listing does not prove the machinery-removal date. The Court of Appeal’s later recital of rent arrears and a 1953 payment must be mapped to the relevant tenancy/parcel before treating it as inconsistent with Mary’s house-parcel recollection. The 1877 instrument, receipt, estate/rent accounts, and exact parcel extent remain unverified.
model_events.status: Family testimony; underlying receipt not located; remembered date/payee conflicts with Alfred Thomas’s independently recorded death on 14 December 1927; actual payee and parcel remain unresolved.

model_events.title: John Williams’s death date must be established before linking it to the 1949–52 sequence
model_events.details: The current John Williams research page records that he was still alive and very ill in the early 1950s, but his date of death has not been established and a death certificate has not yet been obtained. Mary’s later account places her continued occupation after his death. The possibility that the timing of his death relates to the 1949 surrender/regrant, missing papers around 1950–52, or later possession steps is a research hypothesis until the death record and underlying documents are checked.
model_events.status: Death date unknown; do not infer a connection from proximity alone

model_events.title: WGR–John Williams tenancy plan depicts the fields
model_events.details: The extant research catalogue describes the 1939 plan as depicting the eastern fields (working Parcel B) and not the house parcel. The user’s hypothesis is that the agreement may have been used to recast occupation as permissive and could have been fraudulent; that allegation must be tested against the original agreement, plan and surrounding correspondence.
model_events.status: Plan described in the catalogue; authenticity and legal effect remain to be tested

model_events.title: Surrender and re-grant of the agricultural tenancy
model_events.details: Frederick Buckler’s 2 February 1949 agricultural tenancy is placed on Parcel B only, consistently with the separate 1939 Parcel B plan. It does not establish a tenancy of Parcel A or affect Mary’s independent occupation/ownership claim to A2. Separate 1949 attempts to make Mary’s occupation permissive are said by the family to have failed and must be assessed on their own documents.
model_events.status: Family’s corrected parcel allocation; original tenancy/termination papers and 1949 correspondence required

model_events.title: Missing title papers and the later letting decision
model_events.details: Mary’s account reports that title or farm papers went missing from a blanket box around this period; a lodger was said to have taken them at Mr Knapp’s request, which is uncorroborated testimony. The later court history records agents deciding not to proceed with Frederick’s letting in 1952. The underlying papers and any written termination notice have not been inspected, so the exact sequence and causal relationship remain open.
model_events.status: Family account and later court history; primary papers required

model_events.date_text: May 1951 (12 years after May 1939; arithmetic only)
model_events.title: Test the proposed 12-year trigger against the actual tenancy documents
model_events.details: The calendar interval from the May 1939 agreement reaches twelve years in May 1951. The hypothesis is that WGR used this point to end or decline to renew an arrangement and then pursue possession. No termination document establishing that trigger has been inspected here; the later 1952 letting decision is near enough to investigate but does not prove the theory.
model_events.status: Date arithmetic only; no demonstrated causal link

model_events.title: Order 14: Parcel B legal scope; wider physical taking on 4 July 1955
model_events.details: The family’s corrected reconstruction distinguishes the legal scope of WGR’s 1955 Order 14, understood as Parcel B only, from the physical taking on 4 July 1955, said to comprise Parcel B, Parcel C and the northern woodland (A1). The farmhouse and garden (A2) were not taken and remained occupied by Mary asserting ownership. The words “whole farm” in the order were not geographically explained and must be read against the 1916 meaning and the reported 1928 change under the 1877 agreement. The original order, warrant, plan and execution return are required to test this reconstruction.
model_events.status: Corrected family reconstruction; primary instruments and execution return still to be examined

model_events.title: Green south of the house registered as VG41
model_events.details: The green is treated in the current parcel model as separate Parcel C, not part of Parcel A. Whether Williams held title or a possessory interest in C remains open. The VG41 application, map, notice and objection file is needed to determine what was registered and on what basis.
model_events.status: Registration date recited; underlying application file not yet inspected
